doc.title: Roy Haynes — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Early bands and Luis Russell's Harlem
title: Drugs in Harlem and who they were meant for
summary: After a break, Haynes says old drugs were better and that harmful ones were deliberately sent into Harlems to shape youngsters.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Kimery: There’s nowhere to go. Did you turn that off or on?
I’ll turn it back on now.
No, I’m going to leave that alone.

You don’t have to worry. They can’t implicate you. That happened 50 years ago. There’s nothing they can say. And besides, it wasn’t true. What was that scene like though, the whole drug scene? A lot of people talk about it.
You mean back – way back then?

Oh, I don’t want to go too – that far with that, because all the drugs were better then. Now you got a lot of stuff that they make, that they’re trying to replace that with. They’re trying to make you crazy with what they make for you. It was designed for you. That I know.
Do you think that it was purposely or consciously being filtered into Harlem?
To all the Harlems of our country, yes. Are you kidding me? All the Harlems.
For what purpose? To design us to be certain ways, especially the youngsters coming up. To put them in a certain mode. Next.
